# Chapter 1: Pip Has a Problem
Pip was a little red squirrel.
He lived in a big oak tree.
His best friend was Barnaby.
Barnaby was a big brown dog.
He had long ears and a very waggy tail.
One sunny morning, Pip woke up.
He ran to his secret hiding place.
"Oh no!" cried Pip.
"My nuts are gone!"
Pip looked left.
He looked right.
He looked under a leaf.
There were no nuts.
"This is a mystery," said Pip.
"I need Barnaby!"
# Chapter 2: Barnaby Has a Plan
Barnaby was asleep in the garden.
"Barnaby! Wake up!" shouted Pip.
Barnaby opened one eye.
"Is it time for breakfast?" he asked.
"No!" said Pip. "Someone has taken my nuts!"
Barnaby sat up.
He gave his nose a little sniff.
Then he gave a BIG sniff.
"I am a dog," said Barnaby.
"And dogs have very good noses."
"Can you find my nuts?" asked Pip.
"I can try," said Barnaby.
His tail began to wag.
"Let us find the thief!"
# Chapter 3: The Strange Trail
Barnaby put his nose to the ground.
Sniff, sniff, sniff.
He walked past the pond.
He walked under the old bridge.
He stopped beside a muddy path.
"Look!" cried Pip.
There were tiny marks in the mud.
"Footprints!" said Barnaby.
"Who made them?" asked Pip.
Barnaby looked at the marks.
"Not a dog," he said.
"Not a rabbit."
"Maybe a very small elephant?"
Pip laughed.
"Barnaby! Elephants are HUGE!"
"Then it is a very clever elephant," said Barnaby.
They both laughed.
# Chapter 4: A Noise in the Bush
Suddenly, a bush began to shake.
Rustle, rustle, rustle!
Pip jumped onto Barnaby's back.
"What was that?" whispered Pip.
Barnaby stood very still.
"Come out!" he called.
A little nose appeared.
Then two small ears.
Then a tiny face.
It was Molly the mouse.
"Hello," said Molly.
"Why are you hiding?" asked Pip.
"I am not hiding," said Molly.
"I am eating my lunch."
She held up a piece of cheese.
"Have you seen my nuts?" asked Pip.
Molly shook her head.
"No. But I saw something strange."
"What?" asked Barnaby.
"A lot of nuts rolled down the hill!"
Pip gasped.
"My nuts can roll?"
"Yes," said Molly.
"Very fast!"
# Chapter 5: The Big Discovery
Pip and Barnaby ran down the hill.
At the bottom was a little stream.
And beside the stream was a hollow log.
Barnaby looked inside.
"Woof!" he cried.
"Pip! Come and see!"
Pip ran over.
Inside the log was a huge pile of nuts.
"My nuts!" shouted Pip.
He jumped up and down.
"We found them!"
Barnaby looked at the hill.
Then he looked at the log.
"I think I know what happened," he said.
"The wind blew your nuts out of the tree."
"They rolled down the hill."
"And they fell into this log."
Pip scratched his head.
"So there was no thief?"
"No thief," said Barnaby.
"Just a windy day!"
# Chapter 6: The Best Friends
Pip carried one nut.
Barnaby carried a stick.
Pip carried two nuts.
Barnaby carried another stick.
"Barnaby," said Pip.
"Why are you collecting sticks?"
Barnaby looked surprised.
"Because they are lovely sticks!"
Pip laughed so hard that he fell over.
Soon, they were back at the oak tree.
Pip put his nuts in a safe place.
This time, he put a lid on the hole.
"Thank you, Barnaby," said Pip.
"You are the best dog in the world."
Barnaby smiled.
"Does that mean I can have a biscuit?"
"Yes," said Pip.
"Two biscuits!"
Barnaby wagged his tail.
It was a very good day.
And there was only one mystery left.
Where had Barnaby put his favourite stick?
